abstract:
To investigate the anti-lymphangiogenic and anti-metastatic effects of Ziyin Huatan Recipe (ZYHT) on gastric cancer (GC), and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, with a particular focus on the pleomorphic adenoma gene 1 (PLAG1)/vascular endothe lial growth factor C (VEGF-C)/vascular endothe lial growth factor receptor 3 (VEGFR-3) signaling axis.
ZYHT was quality-controlled by UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS, and 3 doses (50, 100, 200 µg/mL) were selected. Human GC MGC-803 and HLECs were used. Lymphangiogenesis, migration, and permeability were evaluated by tube formation, Transwell, and FITC-dextran permeability assays, respectively. Secreted VEGF-C was measured by ELISA. In vivo, a popliteal lymph node metastasis model was established by footpad injection of MGC-803 cells in nude mice, followed by intragastric administration of ZYHT (940, 1,880, 3,760 mg•kg-1•d-1) for 3 weeks. RNA-seq and bioinformatics were performed to identify differential expressed genes (DEGs) and pathways. PLAG1-modified cells were established by lentiviral transduction. Proliferation and VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 signaling related protein expression were assessed via CCK-8, colony formation, and Western blot. PLAG1-driven VEGF-C transcription was verified by dual-luciferase assay.
ZYHT effectively inhibits GC lymph node metastasis both in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, ZYHT could suppress the activity of VEGF-C/VEGFR-3. Transcriptomic analysis revealed 7,739 DEGs following ZYHT treatment. Furthermore, PLAG1 was identified as a critical transcription factor involved in lymph node metastasis in GC through its regulation of VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 pathway.
ZYHT is an effective compound for inhibiting lymph node metastasis in GC via downregulation of PLAG1-mediated VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 signaling. Additionally, PLAG1 may serve as a significant biomarker during the process of GC metastasis through regulating VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 pathway.
